title: core/time/local_day_clock.dart's currentLocalDayClock global has no compiler-enforced set/reset pairing for tests
rule: SM-7 spirit (no global/static mutable singletons) / TQ-6 hermetic tests
why: This mutable top-level variable backs DateTimeFactory, which is called from 15+ production sites across DAOs/repositories/mergers (e.g. track_dao.dart, a churn hotspot, calls it 8 times). Test isolation relies entirely on every caller of useLocalDayClock() remembering to pair it with `tearDown(resetLocalDayClock)` per the doc comment's 'MUST' — nothing in the type system enforces this. A test file that calls useLocalDayClock() without the tearDown pairing would silently freeze time for every later test in that file/isolate, producing flaky failures unrelated to the code under test. I checked the two actual test files that use it (only outbox_processor_test.dart and one other) and both correctly pair set/reset via `tearDown(resetLocalDayClock)`, so this is a latent, convention-enforced risk rather than a demonstrated failure today.
recommendation: Add a shared test helper (e.g. `withFakeClock(seed, body)`) that calls `addTearDown(resetLocalDayClock)` itself so individual tests can't forget the reset, and migrate the existing 2 call sites to it.
acceptance_criteria: A shared test helper pairs useLocalDayClock with an auto-registered tearDown reset
Existing call sites in outbox_processor_test.dart (and any sibling) migrated to the helper
